summary: Opaque pacing window causes perceived session hang during SDK retry surge
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden increase in perceived inference timeouts and stalled streaming sessions across multiple hosts in their dedicated pool. Symptoms look like model hangs because client SDKs observe long tail blocking and retry heavily.

Impact:
- Multiple production customers of NimbleDocs saw 15-30% of streaming sessions stall for 10-30s during a 45-minute window on 2026-03-10.
- Automated client retries caused burst traffic and amplified queueing behind a server-side pacing window, making the issue look like a model regression.
- No model errors (5xx) were produced; gateway returned intermittent 429/Retry-After and then resumed normal throughput.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: prod-us-east (gpu-pool-dedicated-42)
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (Maya):
- Collected SDK logs and streaming session traces from NimbleDocs. Observed rapid client-side retry loops (default SDK backoff disabled by customer).
- Observed a consistent server-side rate-window enforcement interval: short windows where new requests were queued and soft-429s returned.
- Serving runtime metrics: queue length spiked then drained in bursts. P95 latency increased during drain periods.
- No GPU OOMs or kernel faults. Kernel latencies stable per-host.

Hypothesis (Arjun):
- A pacing window (internal rate-window for per-customer fairness) starts returning soft 429s when tokens/requests exceed configured pacing threshold. Customers with aggressive retry behavior produce a request surge that pushes the queue into the pacing window, leading to visible stalls.
- The SDK did not implement jittered exponential backoff; retries were tightly clustered causing amplification.

Evidence:
- Nginx/gateway logs show 429 responses annotated with X-Rate-Window: true and Retry-After header values of 2-5s.
- Traces show client retries begin ~100ms after initial 429, causing a second micro-surge that re-triggers the same pacing window.
- Patchwork of short Retry-After values makes clients loop multiple times within a single pacing interval.

Repro steps (internal):
1) Recreate request pattern using the customer SDK with retries disabled vs aggressive retries.
2) Send 100 concurrent streaming sessions with payloads similar to production prompt sizes.
3) Observe gateway 429s and per-customer pacing annotation.

Next actions:
- Ask customer to temporarily enable exponential backoff with jitter (workaround).
- Adjust routing policy to apply per-route gradual backoff to reduce amplification while we investigate configuration defaults.
- Prepare a small runtime change to increase Retry-After for pacing windows so clients have time to back off.
resolution:
Workaround and mitigation applied:
- Provided NimbleDocs with an SDK patch to enable jittered exponential backoff and recommended backoff parameters. Customer confirmed immediate reduction in perceived stalls (measurements show 90% drop in session stalls).
- On 2026-03-11 infra changed pacing window Retry-After from 2-5s to 6-12s for dedicated pools as a temporary server-side mitigation to reduce retry amplification.
- Engineering will ship a runtime change to expose pacing window metrics and make Retry-After adaptive based on current queue drain rate (target release 2026-03-18).

Follow-up items:
- ENG-OPS TODO: Add a customer-exposed telemetry flag so customers can see when they're in a pacing window.
- DOCS TODO: Update SDK docs and quickstart to strongly recommend jittered backoff; add example config.
- POSTMORTEM: Create a short postmortem if similar incidents occur after the runtime change.
